title: epan: USBHID: add `usbhid.product` dissector table
description:
Currently there isn't an easy way to dissect USB HID reports without
reimplementing a lot of USB HID parsing in the dissector.

Add new `usbhid.product` dissector table for idVendor + idProduct which
runs dissectors on GET_REPORT request/response, SET_REPORT request, and
interrupt packets.

I'm not really sure if this is the best solution. Running dissectors after usbhid has the benefits of not needing to re-parse control messages, for example `usbhid.setup.ReportID`/`ReportType`. There isn't much of a difference for interrupt packets. 

Maybe needs Decode As table as well?

[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25464/diffs?diff_id=1862126481&start_sha=e1fd0bf237be52be2e2ac25a0268ece67bb08d44)

added 1 commit
  • 769d31cc - epan: USBHID: add `usbhid.product` dissector table
[Compare with previous version](/wireshark/wireshark/-/merge_requests/25464/diffs?diff_id=1862363841&start_sha=aeb80ec39ba53df35a34b138833699f4b44b16fd)

How is the dissector going to know HID report payload meaning? You need CONFIGURATION and HID REPORT descriptor in order to properly dissect the data.

I think the only potential improvement would be to make it possible to supply the descriptors out-of-band (like capture secrets), but then still the user would have to get the data from somewhere.

The builtin HID dissector already works when the HID descriptor contains meaningful information. This was intended for when everything is "vendor" class, for example the 2026 Steam Controller: <https://github.com/iczero/steam-controller-stuff/blob/master/dissector.lua>. In this case you can do idVendor/idProduct matching.
Can you attach pcap with complete enumeration of 2026 Steam Controller?

[usb-direct-basic.pcapng](/uploads/9e20de9ac92c54243136e6d2520b7e28/usb-direct-basic.pcapng)

Mouse/Keyboard usages are for "lizard mode". Controller state is sent in report 0x45 (vendor) instead.

HID dissector is not quite doing what it is expected - Usage Vendor Report ID 0x45 (see byte 255 in packet 63) show have 45 bytes vendor payload, but the `usbhid.data.vendor` in packet 65 only has 1 byte and the rest is padding.

What needs to be done is to understand why the dissection doesn't properly put the full 45 bytes under `usbhid.data.vendor`. This PR is not going to change how the vendor data is being dissected, as it does not touch the problematic part at all.

My motivation for this PR is to make it easier to write dissectors specifically for custom USB HID protocols (like the Steam Controller) even if the HID descriptor is wrong or mostly useless. I'm not really sure if this is a good way to do it. Previously I tried registering the dissector under the `usb.product` table instead but that seemed like a pretty big hack and required reimplementing parsing for HID control packets.

I think the solution would be two part:
1. Fix the report parser so it correctly puts all data under `usbhid.data.vendor`
2. Implement a payload handover mechanism to vendor specific HID report dissectors.

What if a dissector needs to handle non-vendor reports as well? For example if the HID descriptor is incorrect or a dissector wants to do further parsing on a standard report. It's not that important for this specific case although I do still use it to write "Lizard mode keyboard/mouse" to the info column before handing it back to the usbhid dissector.

If HID descriptor is incorrect, then things are not going to work with generic HID host drivers.

Do you want just to extend the info column based on Report ID? So here it would be "Keyboard"/"Mouse"/"Vendor" prefix in the info column? I think this could be generic and would improve the HID dissector for all devices.

I think it would be ideal if there were a way to hand off all in/out/feature reports for a specific idVendor/idProduct pair (or some other identifier maybe) to a registered dissector. This would allow users to easily write a dissector for certain devices even if the HID descriptor is incorrect. I think this would be a more general solution than passing only vendor specific reports.

Regarding generic host drivers, Linux does have descriptor fixup for various devices if they ship with broken descriptors. For those trying to debug broken devices it would be useful to get to handle every report. I've previously encountered this problem with NKRO on a Ducky keyboard (the Ducky One 2 IIRC).

If you're fine with this direction, maybe usbhid can attach a new tvb to packets containing a pseudoheader (in/out/feature, for feature reports, report id for get/set, etc) and then copy the original report after that? It can then run usbhid specific dissectors on that tvb. I don't think Lua dissectors are able to access the urb struct so the pseudoheader would address that requirement. Or maybe just put stuff in `pinfo->private_table`?

This is now vastly different from what this MR does. For broken descriptors it really depends on broken in what way.

I think the "having a hand off" and "being able to hand off to lua dissector" are two separate issues. Currently neither one is possible.

The problem with 2026 Steam Controller doesn't seem to be in the HID descriptor but rather in Wireshark HID dissector. Duct-taping things on top of broken HID dissector are probably going to end up not so well.

Sorry, I don't think I understand. The PR currently sends GET_REPORT/SET_REPORT and interrupt packets (enough to parse all in/out/feature reports) to a registered dissector. This works for parsing Steam Controller reports and would also work even if the device has broken HID descriptor(s). This works for both C and Lua dissectors, although Lua currently requires a bit of extra code to figure out what was requested for GET_REPORT because it cannot access the urb struct.

I understand that currently the HID dissector does not correctly handle report length. I believe this is a separate issue that does not really affect this PR, as this PR is intended to work around cases where the HID descriptor is wrong or gets parsed wrong. I can try to fix this issue and send it as a separate PR if you want.
